titulo: The brain: cloud or local, decided with your numbers
lead: The AI model is the easiest piece to swap. In the cloud, OpenRouter gives you access to more than a hundred models with one key. On your computer, Ollama runs with no cost per message and sends nothing outside. The choice is not a matter of taste: it is a table with time, quality, and cost.
objetivo: compare a cloud model and a local one with the same question and decide, with your own numbers, which to use for what.

aprende.t: Why swapping brains does not change the rest
Building the time × quality × cost table
Where the cloud key is stored

hero_alt: A desktop mini computer next to a laptop, with organized cables on the dark desk.

nos.detalhe: The loop does not know which model is on the other side. It hands over the conversation and the list of tools and waits for the reply.

The provider is a contract: it receives the conversation and the tools, and returns the reply. In tests, a fake provider answers with no internet and no cost. Swapping brains means swapping the provider in the configuration.
One key gives access to Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Llama, and others. It retries automatically when the service fails and logs the tokens spent, so you can control the cost.
The model runs locally. It needs a computer that can handle it (memory and, preferably, a graphics card). In the INTELECTO plan it is also the automatic fallback if OpenRouter fails.

secoes.legenda: Cloud for power, local for privacy. You can use both.

texto: Pick a question you would really ask the assistant, preferably tied to one of the tasks in your meu-jarvis.md.
Use exactly the same text in both models.

exemplo.texto: Organize into three priorities: close the sales report, reply to two customers, and prepare Thursday's meeting.

texto: Time it from sending to the full answer. Run it twice: the first call on the local model is usually slower, because it has to load.
Write down the time of the second one.

exemplo.texto: Time in seconds, cloud and local.

texto: Read both answers without knowing which is which, if you can get someone to shuffle the order. Score from 1 to 5: did it get it right, did it follow your style, was it useful?
One short score per answer is enough.

exemplo.texto: Would I use this answer without rewriting it? Yes = 4 or 5.

texto: For the cloud, check the OpenRouter dashboard to see what the question cost. For local, the cost per message is zero; the cost is the computer being on.
Write the decision in one line: which model for what.

exemplo.texto: Daily routine on local; client text on the cloud.

Decision: I use ____ for ____ and ____ for ____.

abas.html:
• Hard question, long text, multi-step reasoning.
  • A computer without enough memory or a graphics card for a good local model.
  • You accept paying per use and sending the text outside.

• Sensitive data that can't leave the machine.
  • Lots of simple messages per day, where the per-use cost would add up.
  • Working without internet, or as a backup when the cloud goes down.

perguntas.p: When does a local model (Ollama) make sense?
opcoes: When your computer can handle it and your numbers for time, quality, and cost show it's worth it, or when the data can't leave.
perguntas.explica: The choice is measured: same question in both, a table, a decision. Privacy is the other strong reason: with a local model, nothing leaves your machine.

perguntas.p: You swapped OpenRouter for Ollama. What needs to change in the channel and in the memory?
opcoes: Everything: channel and memory depend on the model.
Nothing: the provider is a contract, and the rest of the agent doesn't know which model is answering.
perguntas.explica: The loop calls the provider through the contract. Switching brains is configuration; the tests run the same.

perguntas.p: Why run the question twice on the local model before noting the time?
opcoes: Because the first call is usually slower while the model loads.
Because the first answer is always wrong.
perguntas.explica: A fair comparison measures normal use. The first call includes loading the model into memory.
